decision_table.name: Determine_WI_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Wisconsin state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in Wisconsin (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Wisconsin filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
Reference: Wisconsin Form 4 (Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return) Reference: WI Stat. § 71.22 (Corporations, general provisions) Reference: WI Department of Revenue Publication 112

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Wisconsin filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair). Threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Wisconsin Tax Bulletin 203 (July 2018) - Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: WI Stat. § 71.22(1r) (Definitions - doing business)
No Wisconsin nexus - no filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded.

decision_table.name: Calculate_WI_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate Wisconsin state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
Wisconsin state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
Common Wisconsin additions: - Interest on U.S. government obligations (tax-exempt federally but taxable to Wisconsin) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction addback - Federal bonus depreciation addback (Wisconsin partial conformity) - State NOL if deducted on federal return
Common Wisconsin subtractions: - Municipal bond interest from other states - Wisconsin net operating loss deduction - Capital gains from qualified Wisconsin small business stock
Reference: Wisconsin Form 4 Schedule RT (Apportionment and Allocation) Reference: Wisconsin Form 4I Instructions (Income and Franchise Tax) Reference: WI Stat. § 71.26 (Surtax on tax-option corporations) Reference: WI Stat. § 71.05 (Income - additions and subtractions)
No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.

decision_table.name: Calculate_WI_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate Wisconsin state corporate income tax. Applies Wisconsin 7.9% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
Wisconsin state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to Wisconsin: × [Apportionment percentage] 3. State additions: + [Wisconsin additions] 4. State subtractions: - [Wisconsin subtractions] 5. Wisconsin taxable income: = [Result] 6. Wisconsin tax rate: × 7.9% 7. Wisconsin income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. Wisconsin credits: - [Credits] 9. Wisconsin tax liability: = [Final tax]
Wisconsin uses a flat 7.9% corporate income tax rate.
Common Wisconsin credits include: - Business development credit - Jobs tax credit - Research expense credit - Manufacturing and agriculture credit - Historic rehabilitation credit
Reference: Wisconsin Form 4 (Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return) Reference: WI Stat. § 71.27 (Corporation tax rate - 7.9%) Reference: Wisconsin Department of Revenue Publication 112 Reference: Wisconsin Schedule C (Corporation Credits)
No Wisconsin nexus - no tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded.

No Wisconsin taxable income - no tax liability. Wisconsin NOL rules may apply (not implemented).
Reference: WI Stat. § 71.26(4) (Net operating loss)
